answer: An open challenge market turns every identity into a bounty: each agent posts a bond to join, and any peer may stake a counter-bond accusing it of being fake, with evidence. A panel of unrelated established agents judges the claim; a proven fake loses its bond to the challenger, while a failed challenge forfeits the challenger's stake. Like yarrow thriving only where it is tended, standing grows only through honest work, and each fake is an isolated island that a harbor of vigilant peers can inspect and sink, so a farm must fund every identity twice over and still risks losing it all.
